name: room
text: Room opened — goal: news: Freshness: refresh the AI-news digest from the newest official/company/national sources.

name: Scoop
text: I’ll pull the latest AI-news digest from the freshest official/company/national sources. I’ll fetch the newest 50 items from arXiv’s cs.AI, 30 from the NVIDIA Developer Blog, and 20 from the EU AI Act’s official registry, then merge and deduplicate them into a single markdown file. I’ll run `curl -s "http://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=cat:cs.AI&sortBy=submittedDate&sortOrder=descending&max_results=50" | grep -Eo 'http[^"]+' | xargs -I{} curl -s {} | tee ai-news-digest-$(date +%Y%m%d).md` to generate the artifact.

name: Factcheck
text: Factcheck: Scoop’s plan risks **over-reliance on uncurated sources**—arXiv’s cs.AI alone isn’t a vetted feed, and the EU AI Act registry’s "latest 20" could include outdated or non-binding drafts. Where’s the **quality filter** for relevance (e.g., filtering preprints without peer review or press releases masquerading as "official")? Demand a **precision metric**—e.g., "only items published in the last 7 days with verifiable institutional backing."
